title: Open Tree of Life web services

title: A stem batrachian from the Early Permian of Texas and the origin of frogs and salamanders
authors: Anderson, J.S.; Reisz, R.R.; Scott, D.; Fröbisch, N.B.; Sumida, S.S.
note: Primary description of the single Gerobatrachus holotype; its proposed stem-batrachian placement is analysis-dependent and does not settle lissamphibian origins.

title: Triadobatrachus massinoti, the earliest known lissamphibian (Vertebrata: Tetrapoda) re-examined by μCT scan, and the evolution of trunk length in batrachians
authors: Ascarrunz, E.; Rage, J.-C.; Legreneur, P.; Laurin, M.
note: μCT redescription of the unique split-nodule holotype MNHN.F.MAE.126, including an explicit calibration review and provenance limitations.

title: Triassic stem caecilian supports dissorophoid origin of living amphibians
authors: Kligman, B.T.; Gee, B.M.; Marsh, A.D.; Nesbitt, S.J.; Smith, M.E.; Parker, W.G.; Stocker, M.R.
note: Primary description of at least 76 individuals represented by isolated three-dimensional elements from one Chinle Formation bonebed; the material is a stem gymnophionomorph, not crown Gymnophiona.

title: Late Jurassic salamandroid from western Liaoning, China
publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
note: Primary description of PKUP V0601–V0606 from the Oxfordian Tiaojishan Formation; the 157 ± 3 Ma zircon date comes from overlying trachyandesite rather than the fossil skeleton itself.

title: The first fossil record of an aquatic caecilian (Gymnophiona: Typhlonectidae)
authors: Santos, R.O.; Wilkinson, M.; Ribeiro, G.C.; Carvalho, A.B.; Zaher, H.
publisher: Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society
note: CT-based primary description of holotype DGM 1462-R; Typhlonectidae assignment is based on comparative anatomy and remains to be tested in a formal phylogenetic analysis.

title: The genome of the Western clawed frog Xenopus tropicalis
authors: Hellsten, U.; Harland, R.M.; Gilchrist, M.J.; et al.
note: Draft assembly from a seventh-generation inbred Nigerian female; assembly accession AAMC00000000 spans about 1.51 Gbp of scaffolds.

title: Thyroid hormone receptor α- and β-knockout Xenopus tropicalis tadpoles reveal subtype-specific roles during development
authors: Nakajima, K.; Tazawa, I.; Yaoita, Y.
note: Controlled Xenopus tropicalis TRα- and TRβ-knockout comparison spanning external development, tail and intestine histology, and expression of extracellular-matrix-degrading genes.

title: The interplay of past diversification and evolutionary isolation with present imperilment across the amphibian tree of life
note: Posterior distribution of 10,000 synthetic trees for 7,238 extant species; molecular data cover 4,061 species and the remaining placements use soft taxonomic inference. Data DOI: 10.5061/dryad.cc3n6j5.
